description:
Nothing bounds an individual test except a 20 s hard stop, so a slow test hides inside the suite total. This measures every test's duration on main and derives the per-test limits from the measurement.

## Background

`.config/nextest.toml` sets `slow-timeout = { period = "10s", terminate-after = 2 }`, a 20 s hard bound per test. `scripts/rust-build-budget.sh` enforces a whole-suite duration (`MAX_TEST_SUITE_SECONDS=30`) over nextest and doctests together; recent warm runs measure about 22–24 s (`dev/benchmarks/rust-build-budgets/README.md`). The workspace has library unit tests, harness tests over `InMemoryStorage`, and CLI integration tests that spawn the binary, and their natural costs differ.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed benchmark note under `dev/benchmarks/` records each test's duration on main, at a stated commit, from at least three warm runs on a quiet host. The host load at each run's start is stated, and the source is nextest's per-test timing (its JUnit report), not wall-clock estimates.
- [hard] REQ-02: The note states the distribution per test layer (library unit tests; integration and CLI tests), including the median, p95, p99 and maximum, and lists every test above the proposed limit with its duration.
- [hard] REQ-03: The note proposes one limit per layer, derived from the measured distribution with the derivation stated, and tight enough that unit tests are bounded well below the current 20 s hard stop.

## Notes

Measure when no other lead's gates are running, because the measurement and the gates distort each other.
title: Measure per-test durations and derive the per-test limits
